main_text.p: dictio superveniret & condemnatio æ na. Liberationem hanc per Christum depti sumus; gratiâ salvati per fidem ipsum, juxtà Fœdus Euangelicum, Legi illi contradistinctum.

Hinc 1. Apostolus Rom. vi, 14. Non estis sub Lege; sed sub Gratiâ. Ipsa inte Gratia ad Gratitudinem ac novam Obedientiam nos excitat magis; & virtutem Christo suppeditat ad præstandum istud officium; docente ibidem Apostolo versil. 15.

2.1 Tim. 1,9. Legem justo non esse positam, sed sceleratis & subjici nescis, impiis & profanis, patricidis, matricidis, homicidis, &c. ubi Synecdochicè in ratione Fœderali Sanctio pœnalis spectatur. Interim per Christum liberati itâ loquuntur, & itâ faciunt, ut per Legem libertatis dicendi; Jac. 1, 12. non sanè ex rigore formulâ Fœderis Legalis; sed κατ' ἐπιείκειαν & admirandam φιλανθρωπίαν, Euangelicam propositam; quâ ex Plenitudine Christi omnes accepimus, & Gratiam pro Gratia. Nam Lex illa per Mosen data est; Gratia & Veritas per Jesum Christum præstita; Joh. 1, 16, 17. Ut jus illud Legis compleatur in nobis; Rom. viii, 4. Nam finis Legis

page.notes: The right side of the scan is cut off, so the ends of most lines are missing and are not transcribed. Words cut by the edge are left incomplete rather than guessed. Several passages in the visible part are italic or Greek and are copied as printed. The catchword at the foot right is cut off and not transcribed. Some readings, such as "Ut jus illud" and "Gratia ad Gratitudinem", are uncertain at the edge.
